findings.name: Marking a notification unread from the Read tab throws you out of the Read view to the Unread list
findings.summary: The page navigates to /notifications?page=1 — the q=read filter is dropped and the person is dumped on the Unread list, where the notification now appears with an Unread count of 1. Done twice from /notifications?q=read, same result both times. (on /notifications?q=read)
findings.expected: The notification becomes unread and the page stays in the Read view (address /notifications?q=read), the row disappearing from that list; the Unread tab count goes up.
findings.actual: The page navigates to /notifications?page=1 — the q=read filter is dropped and the person is dumped on the Unread list, where the notification now appears with an Unread count of 1. Done twice from /notifications?q=read, same result both times.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open https://5503-iqgs3fdkdmn70ntvor14g.e2b.app/notifications?q=read (the Read tab).
Hover the notification row "eval/harbor-handbook #1 Expand the onboarding checklist" so the two action buttons appear on its right.
Click the bell button "Mark as unread".
Watch the address bar and the list that is shown.

findings.name: Watching search treats "%" and "_" as wildcards and lists every repository
findings.summary: The search lists all three watched repositories (agent13-alpha-notes, agent13-zulu-book, harbor-handbook) even though none of their names or descriptions contain "%". The same happens with a single underscore "_": all repositories are listed. The search treats SQL LIKE wildcards % and _ as match-anything instead of literal text. (on /notifications/watching)
findings.expected: No repository matches the literal text "%", so the list should show the empty state 'No matching results found.', as it does for a normal non-matching word such as zzz.
findings.actual: The search lists all three watched repositories (agent13-alpha-notes, agent13-zulu-book, harbor-handbook) even though none of their names or descriptions contain "%". The same happens with a single underscore "_": all repositories are listed. The search treats SQL LIKE wildcards % and _ as match-anything instead of literal text.
reproSteps: Open https://5503-iqgs3fdkdmn70ntvor14g.e2b.app/notifications/watching while signed in as eval (the Watching list shows harbor-handbook, agent13-zulu-book and agent13-alpha-notes).
Click the 'Search repos...' box and type a single percent sign: %
Click the magnifier button 'Search...' (or press Enter).

findings.name: Pinned notification cannot be unpinned: the pin button disappears once a notification is pinned
findings.summary: After pinning, the row only offers "Mark as read". There is no unpin control anywhere (Unread view, Read view), so the pin is permanent for that notification; the only way it disappears is by marking the notification read/unread, which silently discards the pin. (on /notifications)
findings.expected: A notification that is pinned can be unpinned again - the row offers an unpin control (as the row offered "Pin notification" before), so the pin state can be undone.
findings.actual: After pinning, the row only offers "Mark as read". There is no unpin control anywhere (Unread view, Read view), so the pin is permanent for that notification; the only way it disappears is by marking the notification read/unread, which silently discards the pin.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open /notifications (the Unread list with at least one notification, e.g. the row for eval/harbor-handbook #7).
Hover the notification row: two icons appear at its right, a pin and a check mark.
Click the pin icon. The page reloads and the row now shows a blue pin icon after the issue number, and the pin icon in its action area is gone.
Hover the pinned row again: only the check mark (Mark as read) is offered - no unpin control.
Open /notifications?q=read: the same pinned row is listed there too, still with no unpin control; clicking its check mark (Mark as read) silently drops the pin instead of unpinning it.

findings.name: After signing out, Back shows the signed-in notifications page with the notification titles
findings.summary: The browser goes back to /notifications?q=pinned and renders the whole signed-in notifications page again: the notification row "eval/harbor-handbook #8 agent3-notif-alpha" with its time, the Unread/Read tab bar, the notification bell and the eval avatar in the top bar. The session is really gone — clicking the notification row then redirects to /user/login — but the notification content is shown as if still signed in (seen 2 times: once via ?q=read after signing out of eval, once via ?q=pinned). (on /notifications?q=pinned)
findings.expected: After signing out, pressing Back must not show the signed-in notifications page: the browser should land on the sign-in page (or a page with no notification titles, no bell and no avatar).
findings.actual: The browser goes back to /notifications?q=pinned and renders the whole signed-in notifications page again: the notification row "eval/harbor-handbook #8 agent3-notif-alpha" with its time, the Unread/Read tab bar, the notification bell and the eval avatar in the top bar. The session is really gone — clicking the notification row then redirects to /user/login — but the notification content is shown as if still signed in (seen 2 times: once via ?q=read after signing out of eval, once via ?q=pinned).
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1.
Open https://5503-iqgs3fdkdmn70ntvor14g.e2b.app/notifications?q=pinned (a notification is listed, e.g. 'eval/harbor-handbook #8 agent3-notif-alpha').
Click the avatar in the top-right corner, then click 'Sign Out'. The home page with a Sign In button is shown.
Press the browser's Back button.

findings.name: Pinning a notification that was already read puts it back into the Unread list
findings.summary: Pinning a read notification changes its read state: the row for eval/harbor-handbook #7, which was in the Read list, appears at the top of the Unread list (with the blue pin icon) after the pin is clicked, so a notification the user has already read is presented as unread again - and it is still listed in the Read view at the same time. (on /notifications)
findings.expected: Pinning a read notification keeps it read: it stays in the Read view and does not appear in the Unread view.
findings.actual: Pinning a read notification changes its read state: the row for eval/harbor-handbook #7, which was in the Read list, appears at the top of the Unread list (with the blue pin icon) after the pin is clicked, so a notification the user has already read is presented as unread again - and it is still listed in the Read view at the same time.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open /notifications?q=read (the Read view with several notifications, e.g. the row for eval/harbor-handbook #7).
Hover a read notification row that is not pinned: a pin icon and a bell (Mark as unread) icon appear at its right.
Click the pin icon.
The page reloads and the notification that was read is now listed at the top of the Unread list with the blue pin icon.
Open /notifications?q=read: the same pinned notification is listed in the Read view as well, so it is shown as both unread and read.

findings.name: Read notifications are not ordered newest-first: a 2-minute-old row sits below 6-minute-old rows
findings.summary: The Read list is not in newest-first order: 'eval/harbor-handbook #9 agent4-maya-notif check' (2 minutes ago) is listed below 'eval/harbor-handbook #8 agent3-notif-alpha' and 'eval/harbor-handbook #7 agent4-notif-two check' (both 6 minutes ago), and '#1' (2 minutes ago) sits below the 6-minute-old '#8'. Both rows involved carry no pin, so pinning does not explain it. The exact stored times are #8 15:03:52, #1 15:07:31, #7 15:03:25, #9 15:07:06, #6 15:03:13 — not descending. The Unread list of the same account is strictly newest-first, so the two lists disagree. (on /notifications?q=read)
findings.expected: Rows are listed newest first, as in the Unread view, so the row at the top is the most recent event.
findings.actual: The Read list is not in newest-first order: 'eval/harbor-handbook #9 agent4-maya-notif check' (2 minutes ago) is listed below 'eval/harbor-handbook #8 agent3-notif-alpha' and 'eval/harbor-handbook #7 agent4-notif-two check' (both 6 minutes ago), and '#1' (2 minutes ago) sits below the 6-minute-old '#8'. Both rows involved carry no pin, so pinning does not explain it. The exact stored times are #8 15:03:52, #1 15:07:31, #7 15:03:25, #9 15:07:06, #6 15:03:13 — not descending. The Unread list of the same account is strictly newest-first, so the two lists disagree.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1.
Open /notifications?q=read (the 'Read' tab).
Read the relative times on the right of the rows from top to bottom: 5 minutes ago, 1 minute ago, 6 minutes ago, 2 minutes ago, 6 minutes ago.

Note that the rows showing '2 minutes ago' ('eval/harbor-handbook #9 agent4-maya-notif check' and '#1 Expand the onboarding checklist') come below rows showing '6 minutes ago' ('#8 agent3-notif-alpha', '#7 agent4-notif-two check'), and that #7 and #9 carry no pin icon.
Reload the page: the same order comes back.

findings.name: After Back the Watching Filter still shows the previous filter and re-applies it, hiding the repos that match the search
findings.summary: After Back the address is ?q=harbor&sort=recentupdate and the unfiltered result is listed, but the Filter menu still shows the "Private" radio selected. Choosing "Not Archived" then sends ?q=harbor&archived=0&private=1&sort=recentupdate and the page shows "No matching results found." even though eval/harbor-handbook is not archived and matches "harbor". The stale filter left behind by Back is silently re-applied, so a filter the person never chose this time changes the result. (on /notifications/watching)
findings.expected: After Back the Filter control should match the address (no filter), and choosing "Not Archived" should send ?q=harbor&archived=0 and list eval/harbor-handbook.
findings.actual: After Back the address is ?q=harbor&sort=recentupdate and the unfiltered result is listed, but the Filter menu still shows the "Private" radio selected. Choosing "Not Archived" then sends ?q=harbor&archived=0&private=1&sort=recentupdate and the page shows "No matching results found." even though eval/harbor-handbook is not archived and matches "harbor". The stale filter left behind by Back is silently re-applied, so a filter the person never chose this time changes the result.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open https://5503-iqgs3fdkdmn70ntvor14g.e2b.app/notifications/watching
Type harbor in 'Search repos...' and press Enter (address becomes ?q=harbor&sort=recentupdate, eval/harbor-handbook is listed)
Open the Filter menu and choose Private (address becomes ?q=harbor&private=1..., list says 'No matching results found.')
Press the browser Back button (address returns to ?q=harbor&sort=recentupdate and eval/harbor-handbook is listed again)
Open the Filter menu: the 'Private' radio is still selected even though the address has no private parameter and the list is unfiltered
Choose 'Not Archived': the address becomes ?q=harbor&archived=0&private=1&sort=recentupdate and the page shows 'No matching results found.'
